The workflow that the Claude Code GitHub Action runs from: "Copy examples/claude.yml into your repository's .github/workflows/ directory. The file is a working workflow, not just an example." A settings row for the same reason as the two Copilot workflow rows: it defines how the tool runs in this repository, through the inputs of the action step, of which the page says "Each maps to a with: key in the anthropics/claude-code-action step". The file examples/claude.yml sets no prompt, so an unchanged copy of it runs the action in interactive mode: "when the workflow provides no prompt input, Claude waits for the trigger phrase". A file of comments alone is no workflow: "A workflow is a configurable automated process made up of one or more jobs" (https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/workflow-syntax, read 2026-11-05), and detection counts the file only with a line that is neither blank nor a comment (detection._workflow_has_content). (evidence, rust-v0.149.0, read 2026-11-07). The base instructions of a Codex subagent, a part of its role: the file that model_instructions_file of a role file names, relative to the folder of the role file. The reference's Standard layout: "Hooks | hooks/hooks.json | Hook configuration". A mod, a plugin with hooks that are JavaScript functions, can name only its hooks module there: "modules: an array with one path, relative to this file, to the hooks module, as in "modules": ["./register.js"]. Can also hold settings hooks under hooks." (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins/mods/reference). The module itself is code, as a hook's command is, and has no row. Mods came with Claude Code v2.1.287, after the collection of October 5-6, and none of its plugin hooks/hooks.json files has a modules list. A hook counts only as a handler in a matcher group of an event. Claude Code 2.1.318 drops an event that is no list, "must be an array of matchers; received ...; entry ignored", and a matcher without a list of handlers, "Hook matcher "hooks" must be an array of hook entries" (the strings of the shipped CLI, read 2026-11-05).

A part of every Claude Code plugin, a directory identified by .claude-plugin/plugin.json or a local source in .claude-plugin/marketplace.json, wherever the repository put it. The reference's Standard layout: "MCP servers | .mcp.json | MCP server definitions". Claude Code 2.1.286 accepts a flat map of MCP servers or a map wrapped in mcpServers, confirmed with the shipped CLI and the official GitHub plugin. A workflow that runs OpenCode's GitHub action, whatever the file is called: the page's workflows run it with "uses: anomalyco/opencode/github@latest", in opencode.yml and in the examples opencode-scheduled.yml, opencode-review.yml and opencode-triage.yml. OpenCode 2.2.0 no longer publishes the action: "The OpenCode GitHub Action is no longer published. Remove it from your workflows." (https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/releases/tag/v2.2.0). The tags that the workflows name still contain it, "Existing users are unaffected: they reference tags (`anomalyco/opencode/github@latest`, `@github-v1`, `@github-v1.x.y`), which keep pointing at older commits that still contain the action." (https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/59032), so a workflow that names one still runs the action.
